text: The Patriots head to Buffalo this Sunday for a Week 4 matchup against the Bills at 1 PM ET, but they're doing so with their offensive line in tatters and their quarterback in crisis mode: Greg Van Roten was placed on injured reserve Tuesday with a thigh injury, further weakening the infrastructure around Drake Maye, while the offense continues its alarming freefall, ranking dead last in the NFL at 9.7 points per game following a humbling 35-6 loss to Jacksonville in which Lawrence torched them for three touchdown passes. Maye himself—who threw two interceptions and lost a fumble in the blowout—acknowledged that the offense's performance was "unacceptable" and that he needs to look inward for answers, though analysts are asking whether the Patriots' scheme and utilization of their young quarterback might be equally culpable for the struggles. It's the kind of week where even a high school coach in Massachusetts, Newton North's Nick Capodilupo, earned the Patriots Coach of the Week Award for a far more encouraging performance than what Belichick's successor managed on the professional stage.
